items.title: The woman in the middle of Nvidia spy scandal
items.summary: SINGAPORE-BASED tech group Megaspeed dealt in billions of dollars' worth of the world's most advanced AI chips, and its former director, Alice Huang, was this week outed as an alleged Chinese spy. She was accused of having an affair with Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing. Megaspeed has allegedly helped Beijing skirt trade restrictions by sending Nvidia chips into China.

items.title: Rauf to be sworn in as Melaka chief minister tomorrow
items.summary: MELAKA: State Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh is expected to be sworn in as Melaka Chief Minister tomorrow after BN and Perikatan Nasional secured enough seats to form the state government in the 16th Melaka election. BN won 21 seats, while PN secured three. Earlier, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced that the two coalitions would nominate Rauf to continue leading the state government following their victory.

items.title: NST Leader: White-collar crime invading our homes
items.summary: The latest commercial crime figures released by Bukit Aman paint a worrying picture that should concern the police and the public. Despite the increases, losses from commercial crimes rose 30.95 per cent to RM5.25 billion from RM4.01 billion in the corresponding period last year. Police need to examine more closely why increased arrests and prosecutions have yet to translate into lower financial losses for Malaysians.

items.title: PN leaves Melaka exco appointments to Rauf's discretion, says Idris
items.summary: MELAKA: Perikatan Nasional is leaving it to Melaka Chief Minister-elect Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to decide whether its assemblymen should be appointed to the state executive council (exco). The first step was to win first," he told reporters after the announcement of the unofficial results for the 16th Melaka state election at the Melaka International Trade Centre. Idris also described PN candidates' victories over prominent political figures in several key seats as evidence of public support for the Melaka unity wave.

items.title: Man shot dead at diesel depot in Penang
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: A 41-year-old man was shot dead at an industrial diesel storage depot in Mukim 14, Bukit Minyak. The incident occurred at 4.30pm, with the victim believed to have been shot three times in the body and leg. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim confirmed the incident when contacted.

items.title: Melaka polls: DAP rules out leaving PH despite electoral setback
items.summary: MELAKA: DAP has ruled out leaving Pakatan Harapan despite being the only component party in the coalition to secure seats in the Melaka election. State DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong said the party remained committed to PH, adding that relations among its three component parties remained strong despite the disappointing election results. Relations among the three component parties remain close.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN-PN's identity politics contributed to PH's setback, says DAP chief
items.summary: MELAKA: Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong has attributed Pakatan Harapan's defeat in the state election to identity politics employed by Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional. He claimed that the two coalitions had used narratives centred on Malay and Muslim unity, making it difficult for PH's other component parties to secure electoral support. "They used narratives that Malays must unite and Muslims must unite.

items.title: Macron to make first Malaysia visit since 2017, elevate ties to strategic partnership
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: French President Emmanuel Macron will make an official visit to Malaysia on Nov 16 and 17, marking his first trip to the country since 2017. France described Malaysia as a key partner of France and the European Union (EU) within Asean, highlighting Malaysia's chairmanship of the regional bloc in 2025 and both countries' shared commitment to multilateralism and international law. The French Presidency described Macron's upcoming visit as "a new step" in bilateral relations.

items.title: [OFFICIAL] BN wins 15 seats to form next Melaka government, says EC
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional secured a simple majority after winning 15 of the 28 seats in the Melaka election as at 9.40pm. Election Commission chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the result enabled BN to form the state government with a simple majority. "As such, BN can form the state government with a simple majority," he said at an EC press conference.

items.title: BN-PN sweep Melaka in 24-seat landslide, Pakatan reduced to just four urban seats
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) have stormed to an emphatic two-thirds supermajority in the Melaka state election, capturing a combined 24 of the 28 state assembly seats, according to unofficial results tonight. In a sweeping victory that consolidated the ruling coalition's regional dominance, BN triumphed in 21 constituencies on its own, matching its 2021 seat benchmark, while PN captured three seats. PH suffered major political casualties across the state, losing former chief minister Adly in his Bukit Katil backyard to PN's Ridzuan Sarif.

items.title: Immigration arrest 205 foreigners in Senai raid
items.summary: KULAI: Immigration authorities arrested 205 foreigners in an early-morning raid on several apartment blocks in Taman Desa Idaman, Senai, Johor. Immigration deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said those arrested were from Myanmar, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Nepal, Thailand, Pakistan and India. He said enforcement officers had checked 543 foreigners during the operation, including the 205 arrested, among them 57 women.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN-PN nominate Ab Rauf as CM
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh has been nominated for a second term as Melaka Chief Minister following Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional's victory in 24 of the 28 state seats. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced the nomination tonight, saying Ab Rauf's letter of nomination would be submitted to Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam. "Therefore, I hereby announce that Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional nominate Datuk Seri Dr Abdul Rauf Yusoh as the candidate for Melaka Chief Minister," he said.

items.title: BN-PN sweep 24 seats to secure Melaka victory
items.summary: The BN-PN alliance's first victory came when unofficial results showed that BN candidate Datuk Abdul Hakim Abdul Wahid had secured the Lendu seat with a majority of 5,752 votes. Rauf, who is also Melaka BN chairman, secured a majority of 9,114 votes, a significant increase from the 364-vote majority he obtained in the 2021 state election. Unofficial results showed that Rauf polled 10,293 votes to defeat Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri, who received 1,089 votes.

items.title: Zahid confirms Ab Rauf as Melaka CM after BN-PN supermajority win
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) will nominate incumbent Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh to continue leading the Melaka government following their two-thirds majority in the 16th state election tonight. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the letter of appointment for Ab Rauf would be submitted to Melaka Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam tonight. Unofficial results as of 9.20 pm showed BN and PN winning 24 of the 28 seats in the Melaka State Legislative Assembly.

items.title: Zahid: Melaka voters chose BN's track record and stability
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Melaka voters had chosen a proven track record and stability over campaign rhetoric, Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. He said the incoming state administration would fulfil every manifesto promise. After declaring an unofficial two-thirds majority win alongside Perikatan Nasional (PN), Zahid said the projected 24-seat mandate reflected public confidence in the coalition's development agenda.

items.title: Zahid says BN-PN hat-trick no reason for complacency
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional will not allow its hat-trick of victories alongside Perikatan Nasional in Johor, Negri Sembilan and Melaka to become a reason for the coalitions to be complacent. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the latest victory in Melaka, where the two coalitions secured 24 of the 28 state seats according to unofficial results, reflected the growing momentum of the blue wave that began in Johor and continued in Negri Sembilan. "BN and PN have succeeded in forming the Melaka state government by winning 24 seats.

items.title: ‘Much to explain and reflect upon’: Pakatan accepts Melaka election setback, says state chief
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has accepted the outcome of the Melaka state election and respects the people’s mandate despite winning only four of the 24 state assembly seats it contested, according to unofficial results. Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the coalition would use the results to assess its performance and strengthen efforts to regain public confidence. Adly said the results would also be brought before the PH Presidential Council for a comprehensive review, taking into account previous state election outcomes, including those in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: UTS eyes integrative medical research using Sarawak's biodiversity, AI
items.summary: SIBU: Universiti Teknologi Sarawak (UTS) could become a centre for integrative medical research, combining Eastern and Western medicine with Sarawak's biodiversity and artificial intelligence (AI) technology. Its Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the development of the university's medical faculty would create opportunities to explore new approaches to disease prevention and treatment, including cancer. Abang Johari said research into natural materials could also lead to the discovery of new treatment methods, particularly for cancer, but their effectiveness would need to be scientifically proven.

items.title: Melaka polls: PH accepts voters' mandate, says Adly [WATCH]
items.summary: According to unofficial results as of 9.04pm, PH's Allex Seah Shoo Chin secured the Kesidang seat with 19,781 votes, defeating Perikatan Nasional's Albert Kok, who received 10,672 votes, and Parti Bersama Malaysia's Dr Bryan Kek, who garnered 1,952 votes. In Kota Laksamana, PH's Low Chee Leong obtained 14,547 votes, defeating Bersama's Ethan Lim Zhi Hao, who received 5,097 votes, and Barisan Nasional's Melvin Chua, who secured 1,561 votes. Meanwhile, PH's Leng Chau Yen secured Bandar Hilir with 9,804 votes, defeating BN's Jasmine Lok, who received 2,033 votes, and Bersama's Ir Dr Rashidi Jalil, who garnered 1,304 votes.

items.title: Anwar arrives in Manila to lead Malaysia's mission at 49th Asean Summit
items.summary: MANILA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has arrived in Manila, Philippines, to lead the Malaysian delegation at the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, which begin tomorrow and run until Nov 17. The Malaysian delegation also includes Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. He is also scheduled to attend four summits with dialogue partners: the 29th Asean-China Summit, 16th Asean-United Nations Summit, sixth Asean-Australia Summit and 27th Asean-Republic of Korea Summit.

items.title: Italy fines Meta US$887 million over Android users' data access
items.summary: MILAN: Italy's data protection agency said on Saturday it had fined Meta Platforms €805 million (US$887 million) after finding that the company had accessed Android users' photographs and videos without obtaining their consent or informing them. Meta had access to Android users' photos and videos through a Facebook app feature that suggested content from users' personal galleries that they could post, the authority said in a statement. Meta has 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately, it added.

items.title: Health Ministry reports cyber breach at facility, services unaffected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A cyber incident at a Health Ministry facility involved unauthorised access to a file storage and sharing platform but did not disrupt healthcare services, the ministry said. A preliminary investigation by the ministry's Computer Security Incident Response Team found that the incident did not involve encryption of its main databases. "The incident was limited to unauthorised access to a supporting file storage and sharing platform at a ministry facility," it said in a statement.

items.title: [UNOFFICIAL] BN-PN secure 24 seats in Melaka election, says Zahid
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional, together with its electoral partner Perikatan Nasional, has won 24 of the 28 seats contested, according to unofficial results. The announcement was made by BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi during a press conference at the Melaka International Trade Centre, which had been turned into BN's election results viewing centre. Also present were several top BN leaders and PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan.

items.title: Tok Mat says South China Sea code talks nearly 90pc complete, Malaysia pushing for deal by this year
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 14 — Nearly 90 per cent of the proposed Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea has been agreed upon by Asean and China, with Malaysia optimistic that negotiations can be concluded soon. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said negotiations were in their final stage, although several outstanding issues still required political decisions. He said certain sensitive terms and provisions also needed mutual agreement among the countries involved.

items.title: George Town slashing video circulating online is week-old, man has been jailed, say police
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 14 — The suspect involved in the incident where a man was slashed with a knife in front of Sekolah Kebangsaan Batu Lancang here, as seen in the viral video of the incident on social media today, had already been arrested by the police the day after the incident. The police detected a video of the incident that went viral on social media today. The incident occurred on November 4 and a 30-year-old man had been arrested.

items.title: MBPP shuts 10 unlicensed premises run by foreigners
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Ten unlicensed business premises, believed to be operated by foreigners, have been ordered to close in two enforcement operations by the Penang Island City Council (MBPP). Their equipment was also seized during the operations. "The operation focused on unlicensed business activities, premises managed or operated by foreigners, and breaches of local authority licensing conditions.

items.title: [UNOFFICIAL] Melaka polls: PN wrests Bukit Katil from Adly Zahari
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Perikatan Nasional (PN) has unofficially captured the Bukit Katil state seat from two-term Pakatan Harapan (PH) Adly Zahari in the 16th Melaka state election, according to Barisan Nasional's (BN) election tally. Based on BN's unofficial count as of 8.40pm, PN candidate Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif (PAS) garnered 12,271 votes to take the constituency with a commanding majority of 5,584 votes. Bukit Katil is one of the constituencies allocated to PN under the Muafakat Melaka electoral pact—a political cooperation agreement signed between BN and PN on Oct 29 ahead of the state polls.

items.title: [UNOFFICIAL] Akmal Saleh retains Merlimau
items.summary: MELAKA: Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh has retained the Merlimau seat for a second term, according to unofficial results. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki claimed Dr Akmal won the seat with a majority of 8,726 votes. He said Dr Akmal polled 11,705 votes against Pakatan Harapan candidate Rahayu Hamzah, who received 2,979 votes.

items.title: Anwar lands in Manila for Asean summit before brief dash back to meet Macron
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived here tonight for the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, with a packed diplomatic schedule that will see him return briefly to Malaysia to receive French President Emmanuel Macron before flying back to Manila. He was received by Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Foreign Ministry Secretary-General Tan Sri Amran Mohamed Zin, and Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony. Tomorrow, Anwar is scheduled to attend the 49th Asean Summit Plenary and Retreat sessions, followed by engagements with the Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), Asean Business Advisory Council (Asean-BAC) and Asean youth representatives.

items.title: [UNOFFICIAL] Melaka polls: Noor Helmy retains Duyong with massive 10,067-vote majority
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) incumbent Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem has unofficially retained the Duyong state seat with a commanding 10,067-vote majority in the 16th Melaka state election. According to unofficial party tallies, Noor Helmy garnered 15,064 votes to decisively defeat Pakatan Harapan (PH) challenger Poo Long Suan, who polled 4,997 votes. The result marks a dramatic turnaround from the 2021 state election, when Noor Helmy won the seat by a razor-thin 200-vote majority.

items.title: [UNOFFICIAL] BN-PN claim two-thirds majority in Melaka election [WATCH]
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional claimed it has secured two-thirds majority in the Melaka election. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said this after BN together with its electoral partner Perikatan Nasional had secured a first-past-the-post (FPTP) victory in 21 constituencies. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: [UNOFFICIAL] Anwar's political secretary loses Paya Rumput contest
items.summary: MELAKA: Political secretary to the Prime Minister Datuk Azman Abidin has lost the contest for the Paya Rumput seat in the Melaka election, according to unofficial results. Unofficial results showed PN candidate Rafie Ahmad winning with a majority of 6,008 votes after polling 15,577 votes. Azman garnered 9,569 votes, while Bersama candidate Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar received 1,011 votes.

items.title: 29 Penang schools receive upgrades ahead of 2027 intake
items.summary: Classroom upgrades were carried out at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Bertam Putra, SK Tasek Gelugor, SK Padang Menora, SK Pasir Gebu, SK Mak Mandin and SK Pinang Tunggal. Additional IBS buildings were constructed at SK Paya Keladi, SK Bertam Indah, SK Pokok Sena, SK Sungai Dua, SK Taman Senangan, SK Lahar Yooi and SK Desa Murni. Additional IBS buildings were constructed at SK Sungai Pinang, SK Telok Bahang and SK Mutiara Perdana, while classroom renovations and upgrades were carried out at SK Sungai Rusa and SK Mutiara Perdana.

items.title: [UNOFFICIAL] PM's political secretary trails in Paya Rumput race
items.summary: As of 7.58pm, Azman, the Pakatan Harapan candidate, had garnered 7,867 votes. Perikatan Nasional candidate Rafie Ahmad was leading the three-cornered contest with 12,327 votes. The third candidate, Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar of Bersama, received 832 votes.

items.title: [UNOFFICIAL] Melaka polls: BN bags 15 seats, enough to form state government
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) has unofficially secured 15 seats in the 16th Melaka state election, crossing the simple majority threshold required to form the next state government alongside its Muafakat Melaka partner, Perikatan Nasional (PN). "Unofficially, this completes our numbers — together with our PN partner under Muafakat Melaka, we have succeeded in forming the Melaka state government," he said at the BN election watch party at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC). A simple majority of 15 seats in the 28-member Melaka State Legislative Assembly is required to form the state administration, while 19 seats secure a two-thirds supermajority.

items.title: Man fatally stabbed while trying to stop suspect chasing food vendor
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A man was fatally stabbed at a staircase beside a business premises in Sulaman Sentral, Kuala Manggatal, early today. The 31-year-old victim is believed to have been trying to stop a suspect from chasing a food vendor following an argument between the two over a business-related disagreement. Kota Kinabalu deputy district police chief, Superintendent Syed Lot, Syed Abdul Rahman said preliminary investigations found that the suspect had initially argued with the food vendor before attempting to stab him with a folding knife.

items.title: Police yet to receive further instructions on Shuhaily’s return from border control agency, says IGP
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) Director-General Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain continues to perform his duties as usual as no further instructions have been issued regarding his position. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the police had yet to receive any further instructions on whether Mohd Shuhaily would be returned to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM). “As I have explained before, Datuk Seri Shuhaily is a police officer who is serving a two-year contract as AKPS Director-General.

items.title: Police refer 32 Melaka election cases to AGC, including alleged seditious speeches
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Police have submitted 32 investigation papers related to the 16th Melaka State Election to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) and are now awaiting further instructions. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said 42 police reports were received during the 14-day campaign period, on issues including the tearing down and burning of flags, as well as speeches by several individuals alleged to have contained seditious elements. The 16th Melaka State Election involves 28 state assembly seats.

items.title: Learn from Indonesia, tighten export monitoring to stop under-invoicing, say industry players
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Stricter monitoring of commodity exports is needed to curb under-invoicing, a practice in which exporters declare lower cargo values or quantities than what they actually ship, potentially causing losses in government revenue, maritime industry players said. Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said Indonesia’s move to set up a centralised agency to monitor major commodity exports should remind Malaysia to review how effective its own export monitoring systems are. Jeyenderan said Malaysia already had various electronic systems and government agencies responsible for monitoring export declarations, permits and supporting documents.

items.title: No disruption to border control agency after director-general’s transfer, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: LUMUT, Nov 14 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) continues to operate as usual nationwide, unaffected by the decision to return its director-general to his parent organisation, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM). That is not how it should be,” he told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita Programme (PMK) and the 2026 handover ceremony for the People’s Volunteer Corps’ (Rela) Kampung Angkat Madani (Madani Adopted Village) and Sekolah Angkat Madani (Madani Adopted School) initiatives at Kampung Sungai Tiram here today. On October 29, the Home Ministry decided that AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain would return to duty with the PDRM.

items.title: Equal access to house arrest? That’s not Home Ministry’s call, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: LUMUT, Nov 14 — The Home Ministry acts solely as the implementing agency for the Pardons Board’s decisions on a prisoner’s sentence, including house arrest. Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry was not in a position to comment further on calls from various quarters regarding eligibility for house arrest, as pardon petitions fall outside its jurisdiction. Whether the sentence is reduced, set aside, or the person is released or placed under house arrest, our job is to implement it,” he told reporters.

items.title: 2026 Melaka State Election: Zahid thanks voters for BN-PN’s decisive 24-seat win
items.summary: If the claim holds, BN and PN together have taken all but four seats, which would leave Pakatan Harapan (PH) with just four, consistent with the seat-by-seat figures reported earlier, which showed PH holding only its urban seats of Kesidang, Ayer Keroh, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir. PH has conceded the results. Of the 24 seats declared so far, BN has taken 19, Pakatan Harapan (PH) four and Perikatan Nasional (PN) one.

items.title: Melaka turnout hits EC’s 70pc target 50 minutes before polls close
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Voter turnout for the Melaka state election reached the 70 per cent targeted by the Election Commision (EC) by 5.10pm today, ahead of polls closing at 6pm. Serkam continued to lead with a turnout of 79.08 per cent, followed by Ayer Molek at 78.57 per cent, Tanjung Bidara at 75.94 per cent and Sungai Rambai at 75.83 per cent shortly after 5pm. This is followed by Kota Laksamana at 62.62 per cent, Sungai Udang at 64.46 per cent, Ayer Keroh at 65.29 per cent and Kesidang at 65.64 per cent.

items.title: Wedding day meets polling day as Melaka newlyweds cast votes in traditional red attire
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Nov 14 — A newlywed couple made their wedding day even more memorable by taking time to cast their votes in the 16th Melaka state election today, arriving at the polling centre in their traditional red wedding attire. Yau Wei Ming, 31, and his wife Chan Jia Lin, 27, headed to Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Machap Baru here after their wedding ceremony at a temple. Yau Wei Ming, 31, and his wife Chan Jia Lin, 27, pose for a photograph after voting in the 16th Melaka state election at SJKC Machap Baru in Melaka, November 14, 2026.

items.title: Seven impact marks, metal pellets found: Police probe suspected shooting at Sarikei business premises
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 14 — Police are investigating a suspected shooting incident after a business premises’ metal shutter was found with seven impact marks along Jalan Repok, Sarikei. Sarikei District Police Chief Supt Aswandy Anis said the premises owner lodged a report at 8.30pm on November 13 after hearing seven impact sounds coming from the direction of the shop’s folding metal shutter. Aswandy said preliminary investigations found two fragments of suspected metal pellets on the walkway outside the premises.

items.title: Anwar says legacy debts like 1MDB pushed up Malaysia’s debt, cautions that corruption ruins nations
items.summary: Anwar said the government had steadily reduced its budget deficit since he became finance minister in 2022, cutting the gap between spending and revenue from about RM100 billion that year to around RM90 billion, RM80 billion and RM70 billion in the following years. “It increased because have to pay old debts — 1MDB debt, Felda debt, I have to pay RM980 million per year; Tabung Haji debt, RM10 billion have to pay,” he said. The gap between government expenditure and revenue fell from RM100.84 billion in 2022 to RM92.44 billion in 2023, RM80.9 billion in 2024 and RM76.6 billion in 2025, but is projected to rise to RM80.5 billion this year before easing to around RM79 billion next year.

items.title: PM: Cyber, intrusion and terror threats top Malaysia’s security agenda as attacks hit thousands monthly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Malaysia is currently facing thousands of cyber attack attempts every month, thereby demanding a faster and more robust level of preparedness from security forces in confronting new-millennium defence threats. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that the country’s security landscape is no longer focused solely on conventional military threats; instead, cyber attacks, system intrusions, and terrorist cell movements have become the most critical challenges today. Therefore, we must strengthen (our defence), and last week I met with the top leadership of the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM) to discuss strengthening the cyber security unit within the Armed Forces,” he said.

items.title: Thunderstorms, strong winds to hit seven states, KL and Putrajaya until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds across seven states, as well as the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, effective until 6pm today. In Perak, the affected areas include Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, and Manjung. A similar warning has been issued for Selangor, covering Klang, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Petaling, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, and Gombak as well as Negeri Sembilan in Port Dickson.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB confirms withdrawing letter to Rulers, maintains status quo of Tunku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 14 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has confirmed the withdrawal of the contents of a letter submitted to the Malay Rulers dated September 17 as well as the position previously taken by members of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (MMK) and effectively maintains the status quo regarding the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Also present were the Undang of Luak Rembau, Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, and the Undang of Luak Jelebu, Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi. The letter states that Ismail, together with 10 members of the State Executive Council (Exco), has unanimously decided to retract the contents of a letter dated September 17.

items.title: Slowest seat in Melaka? A look at the Bandar Hilir vote
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Bandar Hilir recorded the lowest turnout among Melaka’s 28 state constituencies, at just under 56 per cent as of 4.30pm today. The seat has 23,042 registered voters, with women making up 52 per cent of voters and men 48 per cent. Chinese voters make up about 73 per cent of the electorate, followed by Malays at 12.9 per cent, Indians at 6.4 per cent and others at 6.8 per cent.

items.title: Melaka turnout closes in on 70pc target with over an hour of voting left
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Voter turnout in the Melaka state election reached 67.74 per cent as of 4.30pm today, approaching the Election Commission’s (EC) 70 per cent target with 90 minutes left before polling closes. Serkam continued to lead with a turnout of 77.21 per cent, followed by Ayer Molek at 76.14 per cent, Tanjung Bidara at 73.99 per cent and Sungai Rambai at 73.79 per cent. Bandar Hilir recorded the lowest turnout at 55.58 per cent, followed by Kota Laksamana at 60.20 per cent and Sungai Udang at 61.08 per cent.

items.title: Foreign minister: Malaysia urges Asean, China to redouble efforts to finalise South China Sea code
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 14 — Malaysia has urged Asean and China to show renewed political will and step up efforts to finalise the draft South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC). Asean and China are aiming to conclude negotiations on the South China Sea COC by the end of 2026. He said Asean senior officials were discussing two proposals under a mandate from Asean leaders at the 48th Asean Summit in May.

items.title: National unity minister calls for year-round community bonding at national Deepavali celebration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Open houses, social visits and neighbourly ties should be cultivated throughout the year, rather than only during festive seasons, said National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang. He was speaking at the 2026 national-level Deepavali celebration at Little India, Brickfields here today, officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The event, organised by the Ministry of National Unity in collaboration with the Malaysian Associated Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MAICCI), was also attended by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.

items.title: After nearly a decade, 647 Sri Pahang Flat residents closer to new homes, says Fahmi
items.summary: Lembah Pantai Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the session, held at the Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) Training Institute, marked another important step before they moved into their new homes. Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said he greatly appreciated the residents’ patience and cooperation throughout the redevelopment process. Fahmi said Residensi Maarof was scheduled to be officially opened by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in the near future.

items.title: Women deserve equal chances to lead in security, defence, Anwar says, citing exam results
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said it would be unfair if women were not given equal opportunities to take on leadership roles. However, he acknowledged that women could also take on physically demanding duties. “While we give space to women, there are also duties where there are many women, in education and medical.

items.title: PM fulfils SK Polis Depot pupil’s invitation, attends school’s Anak Malaysia Carnival
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The wish of a pupil of Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Polis Depot to invite Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to attend a programme at his school came true today when the country’s top leader took time to drop by the Anak Malaysia Carnival organised by the school. Despite his hectic schedule, Anwar said he made the visit to fulfil the invitation from the pupil, identified as Muadz, while also taking the opportunity to personally inspect the school’s infrastructure and safety needs. Anwar said during his visit to the school, located within the Police Training Centre (Pulapol) in Jalan Semarak, he also took time to hear directly from the headmaster about several matters requiring attention, particularly the condition of the school’s facilities and the comfort and safety of the pupils.

items.title: ‘We place so much hope in you’: Anwar urges NS trainees to shape Malaysia’s future
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today told National Service Training Programme 3.0 trainees that the country is placing great hope in them to secure Malaysia’s future. As he ended his hour-long speech and dialogue session with the trainees, Anwar lowered his voice to deliver his closing message. Anwar was speaking during a meet-up at the National Service Training Branch, Camp 515 here where 236 female trainees were present in-person, while another 1,663 trainees at seven other training camps joined the session online via video conference.

items.title: ‘I want to survive as a Malaysian leader’: Anwar firm in not yielding to pressure for policies based on racial dominance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has asserted that he will not bow to pressure from certain quarters seeking to alter national policies to favour racial dominance, solely for the sake of political survival. “Nowadays, wherever I go, people tell me, ‘Anwar, you must adjust the policy, it must be Malay, Malay dominance. Also present were Minister of National Unity Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang, Minister of Communications Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, and president of the Malaysian Associated Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MAICCI) Datuk Seri N. Gobalakrishnan.

items.title: At national Deepavali event, Anwar says govt committed to addressing issues affecting Indian community
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The government remains committed to addressing issues affecting the Indian community in Malaysia, particularly those related to education and welfare, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said the government acknowledged that more needed to be done to effectively address the needs of the Indian community, particularly in education. The celebration, organised by the National Unity Ministry in collaboration with the Malaysian Associated Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MAICCI), was also attended by National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Human Resource Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.

items.title: Malaysia proposes Sustainable Haze Fund, science diplomacy for transboundary haze fight at Asean meeting, says Tok Mat
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 14 — Malaysia has called for a more proactive and coordinated Asean response to transboundary haze, advancing proposals for scientific cooperation and a Sustainable Haze Fund to strengthen the region’s preparedness. “Moving forward, Asean must pursue a more proactive and coordinated regional response, anchored in the effective implementation of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. “Complementing these efforts, Malaysia has advanced proposals on Science Diplomacy and a Sustainable Haze Fund, to strengthen scientific cooperation, sustainable financing, and collective response to transboundary haze pollution,” he said in his intervention at the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting (AMM) here today.
